about.title: Hanford Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Hanford's mix of agriculture, food processing, warehousing, and light industry means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, delivery vehicles, or contracted crews working alongside employees. In most cases, California law channels an injured worker's claim through workers' compensation regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on a road like N 11th Avenue or 12th Avenue contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be available alongside workers' comp. Our team can review the full picture, determine whether a third-party claim applies, and explain your options in plain terms before any deadlines pass.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Automatic
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be pursued separately. We can help you determine whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, while a third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so early guidance helps.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. We can help you understand these protections as you move forward.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near N 10th Avenue in Hanford — do I have a case?
items.answer: It depends on the circumstances. If your employer's workers' comp covers the injury, that's usually the exclusive path against them, but if a subcontractor, driver, or equipment maker contributed to the accident, a separate claim may be possible. We can review the details and let you know your options at no cost to you.

items.question: Can I be fired for reporting a workplace injury in Hanford?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, it's worth discussing with us so we can explain your rights specifically.

items.question: How do you help if I was injured at work?
items.answer: We review the circumstances of your workplace injury and provide guidance on your options under California law, including workers' compensation and potential third-party claims. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only collect a fee if you recover compensation.
